scope: thinkboard-backend only. Extend api/openapi.yaml to the real current route surface (/healthz, /v1/me), install a Swagger UI package and mount it in router.go, verify api/api.json (Postman collection) still matches those routes, and add one integration test covering Supabase sign-in with admin@gmail.com/password through to GET /v1/me. No new backend routes/features, no frontend or Supabase migration work, no change to api.json's existing Postman format.

acceptance_criteria.text: openapi.yaml documents GET /healthz and GET /v1/me (200/401 responses, bearerAuth security scheme) matching the actual handler behavior in health.go and me.go.
router.go serves an interactive Swagger UI (via an installed gin-swagger-style package) at a /swagger route reading api/openapi.yaml; go build succeeds with the new dependency.

api/api.json's Gateway section (Health Check, Me - Missing Token, Me - Authenticated) is checked line-by-line against router.go/me.go/health.go and updated only if it has drifted; format stays Postman v2.1, per the user's explicit answer to the AskUserQuestion in this session ("Keep Postman, sync with routes").

A Go test exists that performs a real Supabase Auth sign-in (or sign-up-then-sign-in) with admin@gmail.com/password, then calls the gateway's GET /v1/me with the resulting bearer token and asserts 200 + a profile_id, using the same NewRouter/config wiring as production.

open_questions: RESOLVED via AskUserQuestion this session: api.json is a Postman collection, not OpenAPI. User chose 'Keep Postman, sync with routes' — openapi.yaml stays the Swagger/OpenAPI source of truth, api.json keeps its Postman format and is only checked/synced against current routes.

The task instruction's admin@gmail.com/password user is not seeded anywhere in this repo (no fixture/migration creates it). Treated as: the test itself performs Supabase sign-up (idempotent, tolerating 'already registered') then sign-in, rather than assuming a pre-seeded account.
risks: No local Supabase/Postgres stack is reachable in this environment (`supabase status` fails: Docker Desktop's Linux engine pipe is not available here), so the new integration test cannot be executed live in this session. It is written to skip cleanly (with a clear message) when SUPABASE_URL/DATABASE_URL are unreachable, and must be re-run with `supabase start` + `go test ./...` in an environment with Docker.

Adding a new Go module dependency for Swagger UI touches go.mod/go.sum — kept to the smallest well-known option (gin-swagger + swaggo/files) rather than the full swag codegen toolchain, since openapi.yaml is hand-maintained, not annotation-generated.
